article.name: Context Mode
article.summary: Context Mode is a local coding-agent plugin that keeps large tool output in a per-project SQLite FTS index and gives the agent bounded replies plus search and resume tools. Hooks journal selected session and tool events; ctx_index also stores files, text, and fetched pages. The review is pinned to the verified current main head. No Context Mode runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

who_what.text: The official README describes Context Mode as a free, local plugin for coding agents. Its hooks, sandbox, MCP tools, and per-project SQLite index run on the user's machine; a separately hosted Context Mode Gateway is a different product.

The official repository page identifies main as the default branch. Its main commit feed reports full head 2065c0ffdf89b0ee88637c5095bff88d6bce0039 at 2026-11-25T03:28:45Z, and a shallow checkout resolved to the same SHA.

architecture.text: The plugin has host-specific hooks/adapters, a local MCP server, sandboxed execution tools, a journal, an FTS content store, and one SQLite database per project. The schema separates session events from indexed sources/chunks; event rows retain session, worktree, agent, kind, tool/key/path, result and byte fields.

The database uses Node's built-in SQLite in WAL mode and FTS5. Content chunks are indexed in a Porter-stemmed word table and a trigram table for paths and partial terms; a line-unit FTS table supports journal recall. Project path identity is derived from the repository's common Git directory (or the plain project directory), while worktree identity remains separately recorded.

ctx_execute and ctx_batch run user-supplied code/commands as local child processes; large output is indexed and the tool returns selected bounded content. ctx_index stores files/folders, supplied text, or fetched URLs. Hooks also capture prompt, edit, command, tool-error, decision, and usage events as available from each host adapter.
The local plugin's searchable store is project-local. The README distinguishes it from Context Mode Gateway, which is a separate hosted service for cross-session/agent features.

behavior.text: Write/index: ctx_index accepts one path, content body, or URL; path inputs are resolved under the project worktree and checked against permitted roots. Indexed text is chunked and stored with source labels and session/worktree/agent attribution. Tool output from sandboxed execution and hook replacement can also be indexed for later retrieval.

Update/correction: the inspected public tool contract has index and purge operations but no update or correction operation. Re-indexing creates source records; the inspected implementation does not establish in-place correction semantics, supersession, or a fact-level history. A caller can purge a source and index replacement content, but that sequence was not run.

Delete: ctx_purge accepts exactly one session, source, or project scope. The source path removes matching chunk/index rows and source metadata; project scope removes the project's event and source/chunk data. The code reports deletion from the local index; this review does not establish deletion of raw project files, backups, copied output, or external host logs.

Retrieval: ctx_search defaults to worktree scope and supports session, worktree, and whole-project scopes, optional source filtering, relevance or timeline ordering, and paging. Search applies scope filters to indexed chunks; word and trigram matches use BM25 and results are combined for project-wide relevance. ctx_resume reads the session's bounded state summary or a journal row by sequence. Retrieved text is accompanied by source labels/headings, not claim-level citations.

Scope isolation: the database is keyed to a project identity. Search scopes are session, current worktree, or project; project-wide mode intentionally includes worktrees of that project. Project resolution and path containment are local filesystem boundaries, not a tenant authorization service. No cross-project or hostile-caller isolation test was run for this review.

Provenance/evidence: journal rows retain event type, session/worktree/agent, tool/key/path, outcome, timestamps and byte counts; indexed sources retain source kind/label and session/worktree/agent. Search output identifies source labels and headings. The inspected model does not represent validated factual claims, truth/confidence state, source passages attached to generated answers, or a mutation audit linking corrections to replaced claims.

Efficiency/observability: bounded output, chunk selection, paging, FTS indexing, and compact resume summaries are designed to keep large tool output out of the model context. Local ctx_stats and ctx_doctor report use and installation/database health; README claims zero telemetry and lists network calls for URL fetch, update checks, installs/upgrades, and user-triggered issue reports. Upstream README publishes benchmark figures from a separately dated/revisioned run; those are upstream-reported results, not measurements from this review.

metrics.evidence: No fixture queries or adjudicated response outcomes were run; code inspection cannot establish answer accuracy or abstention behavior.
No in-place correction contract was found and no correction probes were run.
The local index purge path was inspected, but no post-delete probes or checks of copies, backups, or host logs were run.
Code filters retrieval by session/worktree/project; no paired allowed/forbidden scope workload was run.

limits.text: This review inspected the README, tools and architecture guides, project resolution, SQLite schema/lifecycle, FTS store, journal append, index/search/purge/resume tools, hook dispatch, and sandbox execution at the verified head. It did not inspect every host adapter, policy rule, CLI operation, or all code paths.

The README's published byte-saving and timing figures describe its own benchmark runs with stated revisions, workloads, dates and environments. This task did not reproduce them; all project-defined benchmark domains remain unmeasured for Context Mode at the reviewed head.

The local project database, filesystem containment, and search scopes are visible in source, but the review did not establish deployment-level access control, deletion from every copy, factual correctness, or behavior under concurrent/hostile workloads.

benchmark.note: No Context Mode runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Source observations and upstream-published benchmark figures are not results from this project review.
